decision: Use a deployment-facing identity-bound Phase-1 entrypoint that verifies the qrexec service identity contract before filesystem qualification or any qrexec invocation.

criteria.correctness: Binds intended service, coordinator Qube, non-root service UID, and exact Git SHA before invoking the lower-level qualification runner.
criteria.robustness_security: Fails closed on missing or mismatched deployment identity and preserves the existing filesystem write-denial and zero-mutation gates.
criteria.latency: Adds only local metadata verification; no extra qrexec round trip.
criteria.resource_use: No daemon, database, watcher, WAL, or persistent process state.
criteria.regression_risk: Keeps the lower-level runner unchanged and introduces a narrow deployment boundary, reducing impact on existing contract tests.
criteria.qa: Adds positive qualification plus service, coordinator, UID, Git-SHA, and missing-contract negative tests, all required before qrexec invocation.

alternatives.approach: Modify the lower-level runner to make identity-contract verification mandatory everywhere
alternatives.reason: Stronger globally, but would expand regression surface across existing isolated tests and seams. The deployment wrapper creates a mandatory production-facing boundary without changing those primitives.

alternatives.approach: Trust expectedServiceUid and runtime EUID checks alone
alternatives.reason: Does not prove that service/coordinator/SHA deployment metadata corresponds to the same identity being qualified.

alternatives.approach: Add a persistent qrexec supervisor to enforce identity
alternatives.reason: Adds lifecycle, IPC, memory, and attack surface without improving the metadata binding itself.

failures_lessons: A filesystem capability PASS is insufficient unless it is tied to the declared qrexec deployment identity.
Deployment provenance must be checked before any remote invocation, not inferred from successful transport behavior.
Keep low-level testable primitives separate from the production-facing gate, but make the production entrypoint explicit and fail closed.
safety: Read-only synthetic/defensive Qubes qualification only; no real financial transactions, payment data, fraud workflow, or weakened security controls.
